jp-20261009-news-2.title: Nintendo's European subsidiary fined 35 million euros: The frontline of 'consumer protection' questioned over Switch controller defects

segments.src: ## 何が報じられたのか

フランスの消費者保護当局が、「ニンテンドースイッチ」のコントローラー不具合をめぐり、任天堂の欧州法人に対して3500万ユーロ(日本円でおよそ65億円)の制裁金を科したと報じられています。対象となったのは、ゲーム機本体に付属・別売されるコントローラー「Joy-Con(ジョイコン)」で、操作していないのに画面上のカーソルやキャラクターが勝手に動く、いわゆる「ドリフト現象」を中心とした不具合への対応です。
segments.tr: It has been reported that French consumer protection authorities have imposed a 35 million euro (approximately 6.5 billion Japanese yen) fine on Nintendo's European subsidiary regarding controller malfunctions in the "Nintendo Switch." The target was response to malfunctions, centered around the so-called "drift phenomenon" where the cursor or characters on the screen move on their own without being operated, on the "Joy-Con" controllers included with or sold separately from the main console.

segments.src: なお、制裁金の金額や認定の詳細は、当局の発表や各報道によって表現が異なる場合があります。最終的な内容については、当局および企業の公式発表をご確認ください。
segments.tr: Note that the amount of the fine and details of the determination may vary in expression depending on the authorities' announcements and various reports. Please check the official announcements of the authorities and companies for the final content.

segments.src: ## 「ジョイコンのドリフト」とは
ドリフト現象とは、スティックを触っていないにもかかわらず、入力があったものとして認識されてしまう症状です。ゲームの操作に支障が出るだけでなく、長く使うほど発生しやすいとの指摘もあり、世界中のユーザーから不満の声が上がってきました。
segments.tr: The drift phenomenon is a symptom where, despite not touching the stick, input is recognized as having occurred. Not only does this interfere with game operations, but it has also been pointed out that it is more likely to occur the longer it is used, leading to voices of dissatisfaction from users around world.

segments.src: 欧州では、消費者団体がこの問題を取り上げ、当局に申し立てを行った経緯もあります。任天堂は不具合の修理に無償で対応する方針を示してきましたが、その説明の仕方や、購入時に十分な情報が消費者に提供されていたかどうかが、規制当局の関心事になったとみられます。
segments.tr: In Europe, consumer groups have taken up this issue and filed petitions with authorities. While Nintendo has shown a policy of responding to defect repairs free of charge, the way it explained this and whether sufficient information was provided to consumers at the time of purchase are thought to have become matters of interest for regulatory authorities.

segments.src: ## 争点になりやすいポイント
今回のような消費者保護の案件では、主に次のような点が論点になります。
segments.tr: In consumer protection cases like this, points such as the following mainly become the issues:

segments.src: - **製品の耐久性と品質**:通常の使用で比較的短期間に不具合が出る場合、事業者がどこまで責任を負うべきか
segments.tr: - **Product durability and quality**: To what extent businesses should bear responsibility when defects occur in a relatively short period of regular use

segments.src: - **情報提供の適切さ**:不具合の可能性や修理の方法が、消費者に分かりやすく伝えられていたか
segments.tr: - **Appropriateness of information provision**: Whether the possibility of defects and repair methods were communicated in a way that is easy for consumers to understand

segments.src: - **修理・返金対応の実効性**:無償修理が実際にスムーズに受けられたか、保証期間外の扱いはどうだったか
segments.tr: - **Effectiveness of repair and refund responses**: Whether free repairs were actually and smoothly received, and how treatment outside the warranty period was handled

segments.src: - **法定の保証制度との関係**:欧州では、商品に欠陥があった場合に消費者が救済を求められる法的な枠組みが整備されている
segments.tr: - **Relationship with statutory warranty systems**: In Europe, a legal framework is in place where consumers can seek relief if there are defects in products

segments.src: ## 欧州で強まる消費者保護の流れ
segments.tr: ## The growing trend of consumer protection in Europe

segments.src: 欧州連合(EU)では近年、消費者保護のルールが着実に強化されています。製品の修理を促進する「修理する権利」に関する議論、ソフトウェアを含むデジタル商品の適合性に関する規則、オンライン上の不当表示への対応など、メーカーや販売事業者に求められる責任の範囲は広がっています。
segments.tr: In the European Union (EU), consumer protection rules have been steadily strengthened in recent years. The scope of responsibilities required of manufacturers and sales businesses is expanding, including discussions on the "right to repair" to promote product repair, rules regarding the conformity of digital goods including software, and responses to unfair online representations.

segments.src: フランスは特に、消費者保護や製品の長寿命化に積極的な国として知られ、早い段階から「計画的な陳腐化」への対策や修理のしやすさを示す指標の導入などを進めてきました。今回の制裁金も、こうした流れの延長線上にある動きとして受け止められています。
segments.tr: France is particularly known as a country active in consumer protection and extending product life, having advanced measures against "planned obsolescence" and the introduction of indicators showing ease of repair from an early stage. This fine is also received as a movement on the extension of this trend.

segments.src: ## 企業・消費者それぞれへの示唆
segments.tr: ## Implications for companies and consumers respectively

segments.src: ### 企業にとって
グローバルに製品を販売する企業にとって、各国・地域の規制への対応は欠かせません。不具合が判明した際の迅速な情報公開、分かりやすい修理案内、保証対応の一貫性が、法的リスクだけでなく、ブランドへの信頼にも直結します。
segments.tr: For companies selling products globally, responding to regulations in each country and region is indispensable. Prompt information disclosure when defects are identified, easy-to-understand repair guides, and consistency in warranty responses directly link not only to legal risks but also to trust in the brand.

segments.src: ### 消費者にとって
製品に不具合を感じたときは、まず購入先やメーカーの公式サポートに相談し、購入時期や症状、やり取りの記録を残しておくことが有効です。国や地域によっては、法律上の保証や相談窓口が用意されています。日本でも、国民生活センターや各地の消費生活センターが相談を受け付けています。
segments.tr: When you feel a defect in a product, it is effective to first consult the place of purchase or the manufacturer's official support, and keep records of purchase timing, symptoms, and interactions. Depending on the country or region, legal guarantees and consultation windows are prepared. In Japan as well, the National Consumer Affairs Center of Japan and consumer life centers in various locations accept consultations.

segments.src: ## まとめ
今回の制裁金は、人気ゲーム機の周辺機器という身近な製品であっても、不具合への向き合い方が厳しく問われる時代であることを示しています。今後、任天堂側の対応や異議申し立ての有無、他の国・地域の当局の動きなどにも注目が集まりそうです。ゲームファンだけでなく、製品を提供する企業と使う消費者の双方にとって、消費者保護のあり方を考える一つの材料になるでしょう。
segments.tr: This fine shows that even with familiar products like popular game console peripherals, it is an era where how one faces defects is strictly questioned. Attention is likely to gather going forward on Nintendo's response, the presence or absence of appeals, and the movements of authorities in other countries and regions. It will likely serve as one material for thinking about what consumer protection should be for both game fans and the companies providing products and consumers using them.

segments.src: *本記事は公開されている報道をもとに一般的な情報提供を目的として作成したものであり、特定の企業や製品を評価・批判するものではありません。最新かつ正確な情報は、各当局・企業の公式発表をご確認ください。*
segments.tr: *This article was created for the purpose of providing general information based on published reports, and does not evaluate or criticize specific companies or products. Please check the official announcements of each authority and company for the latest and accurate information.*

jp-20261009-news-3.title: Decoding the 2026 Crop Stockpile Rice Purchase Tenders: Understanding the 'Buyback' Mechanism and the Role of Government Reserves

segments.src: 農林水産省が、2026年産の政府備蓄米の買い入れに向けた入札を重ねて実施しています。ニュースで「入札」「落札」「買い戻し」といった言葉を目にしても、何がどう動いているのか分かりにくいという方は多いのではないでしょうか。この記事では、政府備蓄米の基本的な仕組みから、買い入れと放出の流れ、価格への影響、入札結果の見方までを整理して解説します。
segments.tr: The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF) has been repeatedly conducting tenders for the purchase of government stockpile rice from the 2026 crop. When seeing terms like "tenders," "successful bids," and "buybacks" in the news, many people may find it difficult to understand what is actually happening. This article organizes and explains the basic mechanism of government stockpile rice, the flow of purchases and releases, the impact on prices, and how to interpret tender results.

segments.src: > ※本記事は公開情報をもとにした一般的な解説です。入札の日程、数量、落札結果などの最新かつ正確な情報は、必ず農林水産省の公式発表をご確認ください。
segments.tr: > *This article is a general explanation based on publicly available information. For the latest and accurate information regarding tender schedules, quantities, and successful bid results, please be sure to check the official announcements from the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries.

segments.src: ## 政府備蓄米とは何か
政府備蓄米は、不作や災害などで米の供給が不足する事態に備え、国が保有しているお米です。食糧法に基づく備蓄制度の一環として運用されており、国全体で100万トン程度を適正な水準の目安として、在庫を維持する考え方が取られてきました。
segments.tr: Government stockpile rice is rice held by the state to prepare for situations where rice supply becomes insufficient due to poor harvests or disasters. It is operated as part of a stockpiling system based on the Food Law, with the concept of maintaining a national inventory level of approximately 1 million tons as an appropriate benchmark.

segments.src: 保管期間はおおむね5年が基本とされ、毎年一定量を新しい米と入れ替えながら運用します。このため、毎年の買い入れ入札は、備蓄の「循環」を保つための定例的な手続きという側面があります。
segments.tr: The storage period is generally set at about 5 years, and the inventory is operated by replacing a certain amount with new rice every year. Therefore, the annual purchase tender has the aspect of a routine procedure to maintain the "circulation" of the stockpile.

segments.src: ## 買い入れの流れ：入札で業者から調達
segments.tr: ## The Purchase Flow: Procurement from Traders via Tenders

segments.src: 政府が備蓄米を買い入れるときは、一般的に次のような流れをたどります。
segments.tr: When the government purchases stockpile rice, it generally follows the flow below:

segments.src: 1. 農林水産省が買い入れの数量や条件、入札日程を公表する
segments.tr: 1. The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries announces the purchase quantity, conditions, and tender schedule.

segments.src: 2. 集荷業者などが、希望する価格と数量を示して入札に参加する
segments.tr: 2. Collection traders and others participate in the tender by indicating their desired price and quantity.

segments.src: 3. 政府が定めた上限価格の範囲内で、条件の合うものが落札される
segments.tr: 3. Within the range of the maximum price set by the government, those that meet the conditions are awarded the contract.

segments.src: 4. 落札された米が政府の備蓄として保管される
segments.tr: 4. The awarded rice is stored as government stockpile.

segments.src: 入札は一度で終わるとは限らず、数量が予定に届かなければ、複数回に分けて実施されます。「入札を重ねている」というのはこのためで、必ずしも異常な事態を意味するわけではありません。
segments.tr: Tenders do not necessarily end in one go; if the quantity does not reach the target, they are conducted in multiple rounds. This is why it is said that "tenders are being repeated," and it does not necessarily mean that an abnormal situation is occurring.

segments.src: ## 放出の仕組み：どんなときに市場へ出るのか
segments.tr: ## The Release Mechanism: When Does It Enter the Market?

segments.src: 備蓄米は、通常は市場に出さずに保管します。主に次のような場面で、市場への売り渡し（放出）が検討されます。
segments.tr: Stockpile rice is usually stored without being released to the market. The sale (release) to the market is considered mainly in the following situations:

segments.src: - 大きな不作や災害で、主食用米の供給が著しく不足するおそれがあるとき
segments.tr: - When there is a risk that the supply of rice for staple food will be significantly insufficient due to a major poor harvest or disaster.

segments.src: - 流通の目詰まりなどで、米の価格が急激に変動しているとき
segments.tr: - When the price of rice is fluctuating rapidly due to bottlenecks in distribution, etc.

segments.src: 近年は、2025年に米の価格が高い水準で推移したことを背景に、政府備蓄米が市場に出されたことが大きな話題になりました。この際には、通常の枠組みを超えた運用も行われています。放出された米は、備蓄として在庫が減ることになるため、その分を後から補う必要があります。
segments.tr: In recent years, the fact that government stockpile rice was released to the market against the backdrop of rice prices remaining at a high level in 2025 became a major topic of discussion. In this instance, operations exceeding the normal framework were also carried out. Since the released rice reduces the inventory held as a stockpile, that amount must be replenished later.

segments.src: ## 「買い戻し」とは
「買い戻し」とは、いったん売り渡した備蓄米と同じ量を、政府があらためて買い入れて備蓄を元の水準に戻すことを指します。放出の際に「一定期間内に同量を買い戻す」という条件を付ける方式があり、これによって備蓄の総量を維持しようとします。
segments.tr: "Buyback" refers to the government purchasing the same amount of rice as the stockpile rice that was once sold, in order to return the stockpile to its original level. There is a method of attaching a condition to "buy back the same amount within a certain period" at the time of release, and this is used to try to maintain the total volume of the stockpile.

segments.src: ポイントは次の3つです。
- **備蓄水準の回復**：放出で減った在庫を補い、緊急時の備えを維持する
segments.tr: - **Recovery of stockpile levels**: Replenishing inventory reduced by releases to maintain preparedness for emergencies.

segments.src: - **時期の分散**：買い戻しの時期や数量を調整することで、市場への影響を抑えようとする
segments.tr: - **Dispersion of timing**: Trying to suppress the impact on the market by adjusting the timing and quantity of buybacks.

segments.src: - **買い入れ需要の発生**：政府が買い入れる分だけ、市場から主食用の米が一定量吸収される可能性がある
segments.tr: - **Generation of purchase demand**: There is a possibility that a certain amount of rice for staple food will be absorbed from the market by the amount the government purchases.

segments.src: ## 価格への影響をどう考えるか
segments.tr: ## How to Think About the Impact on Prices

segments.src: 政府の買い入れは、需給の面から米の価格に影響しうる要因の一つです。一般に、次のように整理できます。
segments.tr: Government purchases are one of the factors that can affect rice prices from the perspective of supply and demand. In general, it can be organized as follows:

segments.src: | 局面 | 需給への作用 | 価格への一般的な方向 |
segments.tr: | Phase | Effect on Supply and Demand | General Direction for Price |

segments.src: | 政府が放出する | 市場の供給量が増える | 下押し要因 |
segments.tr: | Government releases | Market supply increases | Downward pressure factor |

segments.src: | 政府が買い入れる | 市場から米が吸収される | 下支え・上押し要因 |
segments.tr: | Government purchases | Rice is absorbed from the market | Support/Upward pressure factor |

segments.src: ただし、米の価格は、作柄、民間在庫の量、消費動向、流通の状況、天候など、多くの要因が重なって決まります。政府備蓄米の動きだけで価格が決まるわけではなく、買い入れの数量が市場全体の流通量に比べてどの程度の規模なのかも重要です。「入札があった＝値上がりする」といった単純な図式で捉えないことが大切です。
segments.tr: However, the price of rice is determined by a combination of many factors, such as crop conditions, the amount of private inventory, consumption trends, distribution conditions, and weather. The price is not determined solely by the movement of government stockpile rice, and the scale of the purchase quantity relative to the total market distribution volume is also important. It is important not to view it with a simple formula such as "a tender occurred = prices will rise."

segments.src: ## 入札結果の見方
農林水産省は、入札のたびに結果を公表しています。結果を読むときは、次の点に注目すると全体像をつかみやすくなります。
segments.tr: The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries publishes the results every time a tender is held. When reading the results, focusing on the following points makes it easier to grasp the overall picture:

segments.src: - **募集数量と落札数量**：予定した量に対して、どれだけ落札されたか。大きく下回る場合は、買い入れの条件と市場の実勢価格にずれがある可能性がある
segments.tr: - **Offered quantity vs. successful bid quantity**: How much was successfully bid against the planned amount. If it is significantly lower, there may be a gap between the purchase conditions and the actual market price.

segments.src: - **落札価格（平均）**：政府の上限価格に近いか、下回っているか。業者側の見立てや、集荷競争の状況を映す指標になる
segments.tr: - **Successful bid price (average)**: Is it close to or below the government's maximum price? This becomes an indicator reflecting the traders' outlook and the situation of collection competition.

segments.src: - **応札の状況**：応札の数量や、落札に至らなかった（不落）回の有無。入札が重なる背景を考える手がかりになる
segments.tr: - **Tender status**: The quantity of bids and the presence or absence of rounds that did not result in a successful bid (failed bids). This provides clues to think about the background of why tenders are being repeated.

segments.src: - **産地・銘柄・区分**：どの産地や区分のものが対象か。備蓄の品質や地域の分散を見る材料になる
segments.tr: - **Production area, brand, and classification**: Which production areas or classifications are targeted. This is material for looking at the quality of the stockpile and regional dispersion.

segments.src: 一つの回の結果だけで判断せず、複数回の推移や、過去の年産との比較で見ることをおすすめします。
segments.tr: It is recommended not to judge based on the results of a single round, but to look at the trends over multiple rounds and compare them with past crop years.

segments.src: ## 私たちの暮らしとのかかわり
家庭で購入する米の価格は、小売店の仕入れ条件や銘柄、時期によっても異なります。政府備蓄米の入札結果が、すぐに店頭価格へ反映されるとは限りません。一方で、備蓄制度は、不作や災害といった万一の際に、食料の安定供給を支える安全網として機能しています。
segments.tr: The price of rice purchased by households also varies depending on the retail store's procurement conditions, brand, and timing. It is not necessarily the case that government stockpile rice tender results are immediately reflected in store prices. On the other hand, the stockpiling system functions as a safety net to support the stable supply of food in the unlikely event of a poor harvest or disaster.

segments.src: ニュースを見るときは、数量・価格・時期という基本の3点を押さえ、一次情報である公式発表を確認する習慣を持つと、報道の意味を落ち着いて理解しやすくなります。
segments.tr: When watching the news, if you have the habit of grasping the three basic points of quantity, price, and timing, and checking the official announcements which are primary information, it becomes easier to calmly understand the meaning of the reports.

segments.src: ## まとめ
- 政府備蓄米は、供給不足に備えて国が保有する米で、毎年の入札による買い入れで入れ替えが行われる
segments.tr: - Government stockpile rice is rice held by the state to prepare for supply shortages, and it is replaced through annual purchase tenders.

segments.src: - 「買い戻し」は、放出した分を再び買い入れ、備蓄水準を維持する仕組み
segments.tr: - "Buyback" is a mechanism to purchase again the amount that was released to maintain stockpile levels.

segments.src: - 価格への影響は、買い入れや放出だけでなく、作柄や民間在庫など多様な要因と合わせて考える必要がある
segments.tr: - The impact on prices needs to be considered in conjunction with diverse factors such as crop conditions and private inventory, not just purchases and releases.

segments.src: - 入札結果は、募集数量・落札数量・落札価格・応札状況を、複数回で見比べて読む
segments.tr: - Tender results should be read by comparing the offered quantity, successful bid quantity, successful bid price, and tender status over multiple rounds.

segments.src: 最新の日程や結果については、農林水産省の公式サイトで公表される情報をご確認ください。
segments.tr: For the latest schedules and results, please check the information published on the official website of the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries.

segments.src: ※本記事は情報提供を目的としたものであり、特定の取引や投資の判断を促すものではありません。
segments.tr: *This article is for informational purposes and does not encourage any specific transaction or investment decision.

jp-20261009-intro-logistics-6.title: [Logistics Management #6] “Even 1 Yen Cheaper” Can Stop a Company: The Reality of Procurement and Purchasing

segments.src: > 購買の仕事は「安く買うこと」ではなく、「必要なものを、必要なときに、総額で最も有利に手に入れ続けること」です。
segments.tr: > Purchasing is not about “buying cheaply,” but about “continuously obtaining what is needed, when it is needed, at the most advantageous total cost.”

segments.src: ## 今日の概念
会社が外から何かを買う活動は、大きく二段階に分かれます。
segments.tr: A company's activity of buying things from outside is broadly divided into two stages.

segments.src: - **調達（Procurement）**：何を、どこから、どういう条件で買うかを決める上流の意思決定。サプライヤ探索、評価、契約、関係づくりまで含みます。
segments.tr: - **Procurement**: The upstream decision-making that determines what to buy, from where, and under what conditions. It includes supplier search, evaluation, contracting, and relationship building.

segments.src: - **購買（Purchasing）**：決まった条件のもとで発注し、納期を管理し、検収・支払いまでを回す実務。
segments.tr: - **Purchasing**: The practical work of placing orders under agreed conditions, managing delivery schedules, and carrying through inspection and payment.

segments.src: 入門講義でよく出てくる評価軸が **QCD** です。Q（品質）、C（コスト）、D（納期）。ここに近年は E（環境・人権などのサステナビリティ）や、供給が途切れない力＝**サプライチェーンのレジリエンス**が加わります。
segments.tr: The evaluation axes often covered in introductory lectures are **QCD**: Q (Quality), C (Cost), and D (Delivery). In recent years, E (Environment, covering sustainability issues such as environmental and human rights considerations) and **supply chain resilience**, meaning the ability to keep supply from being interrupted, have been added.

segments.src: 購買初心者がまずつまずくのが「単価」と「総額」の違いです。実際に効いてくるのは **TCO（総所有コスト）** です。
segments.tr: The stumbling block for purchasing beginners is the difference between “unit price” and “total cost.” What actually matters is **TCO (Total Cost of Ownership)**.

segments.src: TCO = 購入単価 × 数量 + 輸送費 + 在庫保管費 + 不良・手直し費 + 検査/事務の管理費 + 切替コスト
segments.tr: TCO = 購入単価 × 数量 + 輸送費 + 在庫保管費 + 不良・手直し費 + 検査/事務の管理費 + 切替コスト

segments.src: 単価が5%安くても、最低ロットが3倍で在庫が増え、不良率が上がって検査工数が膨らめば、総額では負けます。
segments.tr: Even if the unit price is 5% lower, if the minimum lot size triples, inventory grows, the defect rate rises, and inspection labor balloons, you lose on total cost.

segments.src: ### 何を戦略的に扱うか（購買ポートフォリオ）
すべての品目を同じ熱量で管理するのは非効率です。古典的な整理が**クラルジック・マトリクス**で、「金額インパクト」と「供給リスク」の2軸で分けます。
segments.tr: Managing every item with the same level of effort is inefficient. The classic framework is the **Kraljic Matrix**, which sorts items along two axes: “financial impact” and “supply risk.”

segments.src: | | 供給リスク低 | 供給リスク高 |
segments.tr: | | Low supply risk | High supply risk |

segments.src: | **金額大** | レバレッジ品目：相見積もりで価格を取りに行く | 戦略品目：長期契約・共同開発でパートナー化 |
segments.tr: | **High spend** | Leverage items: get better prices by soliciting competitive quotes | Strategic items: become partners through long-term contracts and joint development |

segments.src: | **金額小** | 一般品目：カタログ購買・自動発注で手間を削る | ボトルネック品目：在庫を厚めに、代替源を確保 |
segments.tr: | **Low spend** | Routine items: reduce effort with catalog buying and automatic ordering | Bottleneck items: hold thicker inventory and secure alternative sources |

segments.src: ### サプライヤは何社にすべきか
segments.tr: ### How Many Suppliers Should You Have?

segments.src: - **シングルソーシング**：1社に集約。数量がまとまるので価格交渉力が出て、品質もそろう。ただしその1社が止まると自社も止まる。
segments.tr: - **Single sourcing**: Consolidate with one supplier. Volume gets concentrated, which gives you pricing leverage and consistent quality. However, if that one supplier stops, your own company stops too.

segments.src: - **マルチソーシング**：複数社に分散。価格競争と供給の保険が効くが、管理コストは増える。
segments.tr: - **Multiple sourcing**: Spread purchasing across several suppliers. This provides price competition and supply insurance, but management costs increase.

segments.src: 2011年の東日本大震災や、2020年代前半の半導体不足では、「安くて優秀な1社に寄せていた」企業ほど生産停止の影響を強く受けました。安さは平時の指標、複線化は有事の保険です。
segments.tr: In the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and the semiconductor shortage in the early 2020s, companies that had “consolidated with one cheap, excellent supplier” were hit hardest by production stoppages. Low price is a measure for normal times; multiple sourcing is insurance for emergencies.

segments.src: ### 内製か外注か（Make or Buy）
自社でやるか、外に出すか。判断材料は、コスト差だけでなく「その工程は自社の競争力の源泉か」です。競争力の中心にある技術を安さだけで外に出すと、数年後に「その分野の人材が社内にいない」状態になります。
segments.tr: Do you do it in-house or outsource it? The deciding factor is not just the cost difference but whether the process is a source of your company's competitive advantage. If you outsource technology at the core of your competitiveness purely for price, a few years later you may find that “there are no people in-house with expertise in that field.”

segments.src: ### SRM（サプライヤ・リレーションシップ・マネジメント）
値切って終わりではなく、重要サプライヤとは需要見通しを共有し、改善やコスト削減の成果を分け合う関係を築く考え方です。日本では発注側が優位になりやすい取引を規律するため、**下請法（下請代金支払遅延等防止法）** があり、支払遅延や、一方的な代金減額などが禁じられています。「強く交渉する」ことと「立場を使って押しつける」ことは別物です。
segments.tr: This approach is not about haggling and stopping there; with key suppliers, you share demand forecasts and build a relationship in which you share the results of improvements and cost reductions. In Japan, the **Subcontract Act (Act on Prevention of Delay in Payment of Subcontract Proceeds, etc.)** regulates transactions in which the ordering party tends to hold the advantage, prohibiting delayed payments and unilateral price reductions. “Negotiating firmly” and “using your position to force terms” are different things.

segments.src: ## 日常の中で
東京都内で弁当店を5店舗経営しているとします。米の仕入先を見直したところ、こんな2案が出ました。
segments.tr: Suppose you run five bento shops in Tokyo. When you review your rice suppliers, two options come up:

segments.src: - **A社**：現行取引先。1kgあたり420円。週2回配送、急な追加も翌日対応。
segments.tr: - **Company A**: Your current supplier. 420 yen per kg. Delivers twice a week, and handles urgent additional orders the next day.

segments.src: - **B社**：新規。1kgあたり390円（約7%安）。ただし最低発注が200kg単位、配送は週1回、遠方のため送料が1回3,000円。
segments.tr: - **Company B**: A new supplier. 390 yen per kg (about 7% cheaper). However, the minimum order is in 200 kg units, delivery is once a week, and since they are far away, shipping costs 3,000 yen per delivery.

segments.src: 月間使用量を600kgとすると、単価差だけなら月18,000円の節約です。ところがB社に切り替えると、週1回配送に合わせて在庫を厚く持つ必要があり、バックヤードの保管スペースを圧迫します。送料は月12,000円。品切れを恐れて多めに持てば、夏場は品質劣化のリスクも上がります。ここまで足すと、節約分はほぼ消えます。
segments.tr: If monthly usage is 600 kg, the unit price difference alone saves 18,000 yen per month. However, switching to Company B means you need to hold thicker inventory to match weekly deliveries, which squeezes back-room storage space. Shipping costs come to 12,000 yen per month. If you hold extra stock out of fear of running out, the risk of quality deterioration also rises in summer. Once you add all of this up, the savings almost entirely disappear.

segments.src: さらに考えるべきは、台風で配送が1回飛んだときです。週2回配送のA社なら翌日リカバリーできますが、週1回のB社では店頭の欠品につながりかねません。弁当店にとって米は「金額が大きく、切れたら営業が止まる」＝戦略品目。ならば、主力はA社を維持しつつ、B社を全体の2〜3割の第2ソースとして育て、価格の目安を持ち続ける——これが現実的な打ち手です。
segments.tr: What you should consider further is what happens when a typhoon cancels one delivery. With Company A's twice-weekly deliveries, you can recover the next day, but with Company B's once-weekly deliveries, it could lead to out-of-stocks on the shop floor. For a bento shop, rice is “high in value, and if it runs out, operations stop,” which makes it a strategic item. So the practical approach is to keep Company A as your main supplier, develop Company B as a second source accounting for 20–30% of the total, and keep a current sense of the price benchmark.

segments.src: ## 3行まとめ
1. 調達は「何をどこから買うか」を決める上流、購買はそれを回す実務。判断は単価ではなくTCO（総所有コスト）で行う。
segments.tr: 1. Procurement is the upstream work of deciding “what to buy and from where”; purchasing is the practical work of running it. Make decisions based on TCO (Total Cost of Ownership), not unit price.

segments.src: 2. 品目は金額インパクトと供給リスクで分類し、戦略品目には長期関係、一般品目には自動化と、かける手間を変える。
segments.tr: 2. Classify items by financial impact and supply risk, and change the effort you spend accordingly: long-term relationships for strategic items, automation for routine items.

segments.src: 3. 1社集約は平時に安く有事に弱い。複線化・内製外注の見極め・SRMで、価格と供給継続の両方を設計する。
segments.tr: 3. Single sourcing is cheap in normal times but weak in emergencies. Design for both price and supply continuity through multiple sourcing, judging make-or-buy, and SRM.

segments.src: ## ✅ セルフクイズ
**Q1.** TCO（総所有コスト）に含めて考えるべきでないものはどれですか。
segments.tr: **Q1.** Which of the following should NOT be included when considering TCO (Total Cost of Ownership)?

segments.src: - A. 輸送費
- B. 在庫の保管費
- C. 不良品の手直し費
segments.tr: - C. Costs of reworking defective products

segments.src: - D. 他社が同じ材料を買っている単価
segments.tr: - D. The unit price other companies pay for the same material

segments.src: **Q2.** クラルジック・マトリクスで「金額インパクトが大きく、供給リスクも高い」品目への基本的な対応として最も適切なのはどれですか。
segments.tr: **Q2.** For an item in the Kraljic Matrix with **high financial impact and high supply risk**, which is the most appropriate basic response?

segments.src: - A. カタログ購買で発注を自動化する
segments.tr: - A. Automate ordering through catalog purchasing

segments.src: - B. 毎回相見積もりを取り、最安値の業者に都度発注する
segments.tr: - B. Solicit competitive quotes every time and place each order with whichever supplier is cheapest

segments.src: - C. 長期契約や共同開発で特定サプライヤとパートナー関係を築く
segments.tr: - C. Build partner relationships with specific suppliers through long-term contracts or joint development

segments.src: - D. 発注をやめて内製に切り替える
segments.tr: - D. Stop ordering and switch to in-house production

segments.src: **Q3.** 〇×問題：シングルソーシング（1社集約）は購買単価を下げやすい一方で、その1社の被災や生産停止が自社の操業停止に直結するリスクがある。
segments.tr: **Q3.** True or false: Single sourcing (consolidating with one supplier) tends to lower purchase prices, but it carries the risk that a disaster or production stoppage at that one supplier leads directly to a halt in your own operations.

segments.src: ## 📚 今日の用語
- **調達（Procurement）**：何を・どこから・どんな条件で買うかを決め、サプライヤを選定・契約・管理する一連の上流活動。
segments.tr: - **Procurement**: The series of upstream activities that decide what to buy, from where, and under what conditions, and that select, contract with, and manage suppliers.

segments.src: - **TCO（総所有コスト）**：購入単価だけでなく、輸送・保管・不良対応・管理・切替までを含めた、その調達にかかる総額。
segments.tr: - **TCO (Total Cost of Ownership)**: The total cost of a procurement, including not just the purchase unit price but also transportation, storage, defect handling, management, and switching costs.

segments.src: - **シングル／マルチソーシング**：仕入先を1社に集約する方式と、複数社に分散する方式。価格効率と供給の安定性がトレードオフになる。
segments.tr: - **Single / Multiple Sourcing**: The approach of consolidating suppliers into one versus spreading them across several. Price efficiency and supply stability are a trade-off.

segments.src: - **Make or Buy（内製・外注判断）**：ある工程を自社で行うか外部に委託するかの判断。コスト差に加え、その工程が自社の競争力の源泉かを見る。
segments.tr: - **Make or Buy (in-house vs. outsourcing decision)**: The decision of whether to perform a process in-house or entrust it to an external party. In addition to the cost difference, look at whether that process is a source of your company's competitive advantage.

segments.src: - **SRM（サプライヤ・リレーションシップ・マネジメント）**：重要サプライヤを取引相手ではなくパートナーと位置づけ、情報共有と改善成果の分配で長期的な価値を高める管理手法。
segments.tr: - **SRM (Supplier Relationship Management)**: A management method that treats key suppliers not as mere trading counterparts but as partners, increasing long-term value through information sharing and the distribution of improvement results.

segments.src: *正解：Q1 → D（他社の購入単価は交渉の参考情報にはなりますが、自社が実際に負担する費用ではないためTCOの構成要素ではありません）／Q2 → C（金額が大きく供給リスクも高い「戦略品目」は、価格を叩くより供給の継続性を確保する関係構築が優先されます）／Q3 → 〇（数量集約による価格交渉力と品質の安定が利点ですが、供給断絶の影響を丸ごと受けます。重要品目では第2ソースの確保が保険になります）*
segments.tr: *Answers: Q1 → D (Other companies' purchase unit prices can serve as reference information for negotiation, but they are not costs your company actually bears, so they are not a component of TCO) / Q2 → C (For “strategic items,” which have high financial impact and high supply risk, building relationships that secure supply continuity takes priority over squeezing prices) / Q3 → ○ (Consolidating volume gives you pricing leverage and quality stability, but you bear the full impact of supply disruptions. For critical items, securing a second source is your insurance.)*

jp-20261009-news-1.title: Miyagi Gubernatorial Election to be Announced October 9, Voting on October 26: Key Issues and Points for Voters to Check

segments.src: 任期満了に伴う宮城県知事選挙が10月9日に告示され、10月26日に投開票が行われる日程となりました。物価高への対応、人口減少、災害からの復興を経た地域づくりなど、県民の暮らしに直結するテーマが論点になるとみられます。この記事では、選挙の基本的な仕組みと、有権者が情報を見る際のポイントを中立的な立場で整理します。
segments.tr: The Miyagi gubernatorial election, held due to the expiration of the current term, will be officially announced on October 9, with voting and ballot counting scheduled for October 26. Issues directly affecting the lives of residents, such as responses to rising prices, population decline, and regional development following recovery from disasters, are expected to be the main points of contention. This article organizes the basic mechanisms of the election and points for voters to consider when reviewing information from a neutral standpoint.

segments.src: > 最新の候補者情報や日程の詳細は、宮城県選挙管理委員会や各市区町村の選挙管理委員会の公式発表をご確認ください。
segments.tr: > Please check the official announcements from the Miyagi Prefectural Election Administration Commission or the election administration commissions of each municipality for the latest candidate information and detailed schedules.

segments.src: ## 知事選の基本日程
segments.tr: ## Basic Schedule for the Gubernatorial Election

segments.src: | 項目 | 内容 |
| 告示日 | 10月9日 |
| 投開票日 | 10月26日 |
| 選挙の種類 | 任期満了に伴う都道府県知事選挙 |
segments.tr: | Type of Election | Prefectural Gubernatorial Election due to term expiration |

segments.src: 告示日から投票日前日までが選挙運動の期間です。期日前投票は告示の翌日から投票日の前日まで可能で、仕事や用事で当日の投票が難しい人も利用できます。投票所の場所や受付時間は自治体ごとに異なるため、自宅に届く「投票所入場券」で確認しておくと安心です。
segments.tr: The campaign period runs from the announcement date until the day before the election. Early voting is available from the day after the announcement until the day before the election, which can be used by those who have difficulty voting on the actual day due to work or other commitments. Since the location and reception hours of polling stations vary by municipality, it is safe to check the "polling station admission ticket" sent to your home.

segments.src: ## 知事の役割とは
segments.tr: ## What is the Role of the Governor?

segments.src: 都道府県知事は、県の予算の編成や条例案の提出、県職員の統括など、県政全体の執行を担う立場です。医療・福祉、教育、道路やインフラ整備、防災、産業振興など、身近な行政サービスの多くが県の施策と関わっています。市町村と連携しながら地域課題に対応する役割も大きく、誰が知事を務めるかは日々の暮らしに間接的に影響します。
segments.tr: The prefectural governor is responsible for executing the entire prefectural administration, including compiling the prefectural budget, submitting ordinances, and overseeing prefectural staff. Many familiar administrative services, such as medical care, welfare, education, road and infrastructure development, disaster prevention, and industrial promotion, are related to prefectural policies. The role of coordinating with municipalities to address regional issues is also significant, and who serves as governor indirectly affects daily life.

segments.src: ## 今回注目される主な論点
segments.tr: ## Main Issues of Focus This Time

segments.src: ### 1. 物価高への対応
食料品やエネルギー価格の上昇が続くなか、家計や中小企業への支援のあり方が関心を集めています。県としてできることには、国の施策と連動した支援、地域の事業者への資金繰り支援、公共料金に関わる負担軽減策などがあります。ただし、財源には限りがあるため、「何を優先し、どう持続させるのか」という具体性を見ることが大切です。
segments.tr: As food and energy prices continue to rise, there is growing interest in how to support households and small to medium-sized businesses. What the prefecture can do includes support linked to national policies, financing support for local businesses, and measures to reduce the burden of public utility charges. However, since financial resources are limited, it is important to look at the specifics of "what is prioritized and how it will be sustained."

segments.src: ### 2. 人口減少と地域の担い手
全国的な課題である人口減少は、宮城県でも例外ではありません。仙台市を中心とする都市部と、沿岸部や中山間地域では、人口動態や抱える課題が大きく異なります。
segments.tr: Population decline, a nationwide issue, is no exception in Miyagi Prefecture. The demographic trends and challenges faced by urban areas centered on Sendai City differ significantly from those in coastal and mountainous areas.

segments.src: - 若い世代の県内定着や転入の促進
segments.tr: - Promoting the settlement and relocation of the younger generation within the prefecture

segments.src: - 子育て支援や教育環境の充実
segments.tr: - Enhancing childcare support and educational environments

segments.src: - 地域の働き口や賃金水準の向上
segments.tr: - Improving local job opportunities and wage levels

segments.src: - 医療・交通など生活基盤の維持
segments.tr: - Maintaining living infrastructure such as medical care and transportation

segments.src: こうした分野で、都市部と地方の双方にどう目配りするのかが論点になります。
segments.tr: How to pay attention to both urban and rural areas in these fields will be a point of discussion.

segments.src: ### 3. 震災後の地域づくりと防災
segments.tr: ### 3. Post-Disaster Regional Development and Disaster Prevention

segments.src: 東日本大震災から十数年が経過し、復旧・復興の段階から、地域の活力を取り戻す「その先」の取り組みが問われています。あわせて、近年は豪雨災害や地震への備えも重要性を増しています。
segments.tr: More than a decade has passed since the Great East Japan Earthquake, and the focus is shifting from the recovery and reconstruction phase to initiatives for "what comes next" to restore regional vitality. At the same time, preparedness for heavy rain disasters and earthquakes has become increasingly important in recent years.

segments.src: - 防災・減災対策の継続的な強化
segments.tr: - Continuous strengthening of disaster prevention and mitigation measures

segments.src: - 震災の経験や教訓の継承
segments.tr: - Passing on the experiences and lessons of the disaster

segments.src: - 沿岸部の産業やなりわいの再生
segments.tr: - Revitalizing industries and livelihoods in coastal areas

segments.src: - 避難体制や地域コミュニティの維持
segments.tr: - Maintaining evacuation systems and local communities

segments.src: ### 4. 産業・雇用・財政運営
県内の産業振興や企業誘致、農林水産業の支援、再生可能エネルギーをめぐる取り組みなども、選挙で議論されやすいテーマです。あわせて、限られた財源のなかで施策の優先順位をどう決めるのか、財政の健全性をどう保つのかも見逃せない視点です。
segments.tr: Industrial promotion within the prefecture, attracting companies, supporting agriculture, forestry, and fisheries, and initiatives surrounding renewable energy are also themes likely to be discussed in the election. At the same time, how to determine the priority of policies within limited financial resources and how to maintain fiscal soundness are also perspectives that cannot be overlooked.

segments.src: ## 有権者が情報を見る際のポイント
segments.tr: ## Points for Voters When Reviewing Information

segments.src: 選挙では、多くの情報が短期間に飛び交います。判断の材料を整理するために、次の点を意識してみてください。
segments.tr: During an election, a lot of information flies around in a short period. To organize the materials for your judgment, try to be conscious of the following points.

segments.src: 1. **公約の「具体性」を確認する**　目標だけでなく、財源・時期・実施方法がどこまで示されているかを見ましょう。
segments.tr: 1. **Check the "concreteness" of campaign pledges.** Look at how much the funding, timing, and implementation methods are indicated, not just the goals.

segments.src: 2. **実績と課題を分けて考える**　これまでの県政の評価と、これからの政策提案は別の問題です。どちらも確認すると判断しやすくなります。
segments.tr: 2. **Think about achievements and issues separately.** Evaluation of the prefectural administration so far and proposals for future policies are separate issues. It becomes easier to judge if you check both.

segments.src: 3. **一次情報に当たる**　選挙公報、候補者の公式サイト、公開討論会や政見放送など、本人が発信する情報を基本にしましょう。
segments.tr: 3. **Go to primary sources.** Base your judgment on information issued by the candidates themselves, such as election bulletins, official websites of candidates, public debates, and political broadcasts.

segments.src: 4. **自分の暮らしに関係する分野を軸にする**　子育て、介護、仕事、防災など、自分や家族にとって重要な分野から比べると整理しやすくなります。
segments.tr: 4. **Make fields related to your own life the axis.** It becomes easier to organize if you compare from fields important to you and your family, such as childcare, nursing care, work, and disaster prevention.

segments.src: 5. **SNSの情報は出所を確かめる**　切り取られた発言や真偽不明の情報が拡散することがあります。共有する前に、信頼できる報道や公的機関の情報で確認する習慣が大切です。
segments.tr: 5. **Verify the source of information on social media.** Snippets of statements or unverified information may spread. It is important to have the habit of checking with reliable news reports or information from public institutions before sharing.

segments.src: ## 投票率と地方選挙の意味
segments.tr: ## Voter Turnout and the Meaning of Local Elections

segments.src: 地方選挙では、国政選挙に比べて投票率が低くなりやすい傾向があります。しかし、県の予算や政策の方向性を決める首長を選ぶ機会であり、一人ひとりの一票が地域の将来に反映されます。投票にあたっては、次の点を押さえておくとスムーズです。
segments.tr: In local elections, voter turnout tends to be lower than in national elections. However, it is an opportunity to choose the head of the local government who determines the direction of the prefecture's budget and policies, and each person's vote is reflected in the future of the region. When voting, it is helpful to keep the following points in mind.

segments.src: - 投票日は10月26日（期日前投票は告示の翌日から可能）
segments.tr: - The voting day is October 26 (early voting is possible from the day after the announcement)

segments.src: - 投票所入場券とともに、本人確認ができるものを持参すると安心
segments.tr: - It is safe to bring something that can verify your identity along with your polling station admission ticket

segments.src: - 当日投票が難しい場合は、期日前投票を活用する
segments.tr: - If it is difficult to vote on the day, utilize early voting

segments.src: - 事情により投票所へ行くのが難しい場合の制度（不在者投票など）は、選挙管理委員会に確認する
segments.tr: - For systems where it is difficult to go to the polling station due to circumstances (such as absentee voting), check with the Election Administration Commission

segments.src: ## まとめ
宮城県知事選は、物価高対策、人口減少、震災後の地域づくり、防災、産業振興といった、県民の暮らしに近いテーマが問われる選挙です。候補者の主張を比較する際は、スローガンだけでなく、具体的な内容や実現可能性に目を向けることが重要です。公式情報を基に、自分なりの判断軸を持って投票に臨みましょう。
segments.tr: The Miyagi gubernatorial election is an election where themes close to the lives of residents, such as measures against rising prices, population decline, post-disaster regional development, disaster prevention, and industrial promotion, are questioned. When comparing candidates' claims, it is important to look not only at slogans but also at concrete content and feasibility. Based on official information, let's go to the polls with your own judgment axis.
